note: The symptom of #3927 is that a texture/sampler pair whose sampled value cannot affect any output (every path through main ends in OpKill) still consumes a descriptor binding in the emitted SPIR-V. So the predicate reads the CONTENT of the module, not the exit code. Clause 2 and 3 are the symptom: `OpDecorate %Tex0 Binding` / `OpDecorate %SS0 Binding` survive, exactly the two lines the reporter quoted. Clause 1 is a positive anchor and is NOT optional: 'a binding is present' is a claim only a successful SPIR-V codegen can make, and the mirror predicate ('the binding is gone') would be satisfied for free by any compile that emitted nothing at all -- a release with no SPIR-V backend, a parse error, a crash. Requiring `OpEntryPoint Fragment %main` means every scored probe demonstrably produced a fragment-stage module. CONTROLS, both captured in this directory: (a) control-unused.hlsl is the same shader with the Tex0 sample and the branch removed, so Tex0/SS0 are declared but genuinely unreferenced and DXC's dead-variable elimination does remove them -- it compiles cleanly, emits OpEntryPoint, and scores no-match, which proves the predicate is not simply matching 'a shader that declares Tex0' or 'a successful -spirv compile' (variant-control-unused-main-debug.txt, --expect no-match). (b) control-hello.hlsl is a trivial `-spirv` pixel shader used as a SPIR-V-backend-presence control on the releases that reject the repro, proving the rejection is the missing backend rather than anything about this repro (variant-control-hello-*.txt). A third capture, variant-O0-main-debug.txt, re-runs the repro at -O0 with --expect match: no spirv-opt runs there, so all four resources survive and the predicate still fires -- which is why the primary probe deliberately uses the reporter's default optimisation level, where the optimiser removes Tex1/SS1 and stops.
